itinerary.cal: Jun-Sep. The traverse under the north face can be snowy and glide-cracked early in the season.

days.note: Leave Alpental and follow the Northeast Buttress approach, then traverse west beneath the north face to the base of the 220 ft entrance couloir in 2-2.5 hours. Climb for 3-4 hours to the summit. Descend the south-side couloir into the narrow rappel gully and back to the Chair Peak basin in 1-2 hours, then hike out.
days.title: Climb the West Ridge from Alpental
days.objective: Summit Chair Peak and return to Alpental

itinerary.totalNote: A long day from Alpental: a 2-2.5 hour approach under the north face, 3-4 hours of climbing to the summit, and a 1-2 hour descent by the south-side couloir.

days.note: Long single push from the North Fork Sauk trailhead, or split over two days with a camp near Curry Gap or on the ridge. Mike Heath's 1968 first-ascent account describes the outing from the road's end as taking about 4-5 hours, though this reflects a fast/direct climb rather than a typical modern car-to-car day given the approach length.

days.title: Day trip

itinerary.cal: The route is in season from late May through June and is commonly done as a 2-3 day trip. An optional middle day can tag Gunn Peak or Tailgunner Peak from camp.

days.note: Hike and bushwhack from the Barclay Lake Trailhead to camp near Tailgunner Pass, about 3,200-3,400 ft of gain and roughly 6-7 hours.
days.title: Bushwhack to Tailgunner Pass camp

days.note: Climb Wing Peak's northwest ridge from camp in about 2.5 hours, then descend all the way to the trailhead in about 4 hours.
days.title: Climb Wing Peak and descend

itinerary.totalNote: Hike and bushwhack to camp near Tailgunner Pass, then climb Wing Peak's northwest ridge and descend to the Barclay Lake trailhead.
